title: Stored procedures and triggers
summary: Encapsulate logic in procs, handle parameters and errors, and use triggers judiciously.

items: Create parameterized stored procedures with error handling.
Use DML and DDL triggers and understand inserted/deleted tables.

blocks.body: Procedures centralize business logic; triggers react to data changes but can hide behavior.

terms.definition: A precompiled batch of T-SQL invoked by name with parameters.
Code that fires on INSERT/UPDATE/DELETE; sees inserted and deleted pseudo-tables.

blocks.body: Triggers access the **`inserted`** and **`deleted`** virtual tables. AFTER triggers run post-operation; INSTEAD OF triggers replace it (common on views). Keep trigger logic set-based and short.

items.fix: Triggers fire once per statement, not per row — always write set-based logic over inserted/deleted.

tips: INSTEAD OF triggers make otherwise non-updatable views updatable.

blocks.body: Use procs for encapsulation and triggers sparingly, always set-based, using inserted/deleted.
